newsitem.title: India: Bombay shares rally on short-covering, ITC surges.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares rally on short-covering, ITC surges.

text.p: ** (1015 GMT) - Bombay blue chips stage late rally
** Bombay stocks index closes 44.80 pts, or 1.32 pct, to
3,427.54 provisional, off 3,464.58
** Foreign funds scattered buyers in pivotal stocks
** Market activity focussed on ITC, leads market rally
** Shares of ITC spurt 4.66 pct at National Stock Exchange,
up 1.4 pct at Bombay bourse, huge short-covering
** National Stock Exchange index gains 2.68 pct to 986.25
** All bourses closed on Thursday due to national holiday
Speculative interest and huge short-covering in pivotal stocks helped Bombay bourses stage an impressive rally towards close on Wednesday, dealers said.
Action was focussed on tobacco conglomerate ITC, they said.
"The market was pushed up by speculative factors...heavy volumes in ITC shares," said chief dealer Sanjeev Choithani at brokerage Pashupati Advani.

The ITC stock notched up a gain of 5.50 rupees to end at 401.0 rupees at the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE). At the National Stock Exchange (NSE), ITC advanced 18.05 rupees, or 4.66 percent to 405.05 in volumes of 9.56 million shares.
Traders said an auction of shares, short-sold by market players, scheduled later on Wednesday by the NSE was the main factor driving the rally.
ITC headed the auction list with 682,800 shares, followed by SBI 54,750 shares and Reliance 53,200.
The BSE's top 30-share index hit an intra-day high of 3,464.58, but ended at 3,427.54 rallying by 44.80 points, or 1.32 percent over Tuesday's close.
Dealers said foreign funds were moderate buyers in index-linked stocks, but local funds remained on the sidelines.
Top Indian financier Uday Kotak said on Wednesday he saw falling real interest rates driving up Indian stock markets.
"The way people will look at equities and real estate will change," Kotak, vice chairman of Kotak Mahindra Finance Ltd told Reuters in an interview.
Reliance added 12.20 rupees to 248.25, ACC 22.0 to 1,347.0, SBI 2.0 to 277.0, TISCO 4.0 to 190.25, BSES 5.25 to 221.0, MTNL 3.25 to 242.25 and Ranbaxy 13.0 to 610.0.
Banks and stock exchanges across India, including the BSE and the NSE, are closed on January 23 for a national holiday.
-- ANSHUMAN DAGA, Bombay equities desk +91-22-265 9000
